Where it began

Sam Curran was born in Northampton on 3 June 1998, while his father, Kevin Curran, the former Zimbabwe Test cricketer, was playing county cricket for Northamptonshire. He was the youngest of three brothers, and the game ran right through the house: Tom went on to play for Surrey and England, and Ben batted for Zimbabwe.

Sam grew up in Zimbabwe, on the family farm at Rusape, and went to school at Springvale House and St George's College in Harare. In 2012 he came to England and Wellington College, and from there to Surrey. He was 17 when he first played for them, and in his first County Championship match, against Kent at The Oval in July 2015, he took 5 for 101. Only Tony Lock had played first-class cricket for Surrey younger.

The player

He came into the England Test side at Headingley in June 2018, and that summer against India he made his name. At Edgbaston he took the wickets of India's top three in the first innings, then made 63 in the second and was player of the match. Later in the series he top-scored with 78 at Southampton, and by the end England had won 4-1 and he was their player of the series, with 272 runs and 11 wickets.

In all he played 24 Tests between 2018 and 2021, taking 47 wickets at 35.51, with a best of 4 for 58 in South Africa, and scoring 815 runs at 24.70 with three fifties. The white-ball game gave him his biggest days. At the 2022 T20 World Cup he took five wickets against Afghanistan, the first such haul by an England player in T20 internationals, then 3 for 12 in the final against Pakistan, and was named player of the tournament as England took the title.

What made him special

He was the sort of cricketer captains love to have around: a medium-fast bowler and a free-hitting left-handed batter who seemed to turn up when the game needed something. He took a hat-trick in only his second match in the Indian Premier League, and in January 2026 he took another for England in a T20 international in Sri Lanka.

The one thing that never quite arrived in Tests was a hundred. The 78 at Southampton was as close as he came, though for Surrey in 2022 he showed what might have been by reaching three figures in 62 balls.

Away from the middle

After that 2018 summer the Cricket Writers' Club named him its young cricketer of the year. He became a Wisden Cricketer of the Year, and was appointed MBE in 2023 for services to cricket. He won the Indian Premier League with Chennai Super Kings in 2021 and played for teams from Auckland to the Oval Invincibles.

And finally

At the 2023 World Cup his first ball brought a wicket, something no English bowler had managed on World Cup debut. As the youngest of three cricketing brothers, he had presumably learned early that you make the most of your turn.
